summary:
Public Law 119-46 (H.J. Res. 133) is a joint resolution requesting the Secretary of the Interior to authorize specific, temporary displays on the National Mall and the Washington Monument to initiate the commemoration of the United States Semiquincentennial. 

The resolution's operative mechanism consists of two formal requests by Congress. First, it requests the Secretary of the Interior to authorize unique and one-time arrangements for the display of United States semiquincentennial materials and other significant artifacts, digital content, film footage, and associated audio and imagery in and around the vicinity of the National Mall. This authorization includes projecting such content onto the surface of the Washington Monument for five nights of public display. The authorization is strictly time-limited, applying only during the period beginning on December 31, 2025, and ending on January 5, 2026. 

Second, the resolution respectfully requests that the Clerk of the House of Representatives transmit an enrolled copy of the resolution to the Secretary of the Interior and the Chair of the United States Semiquincentennial Commission.

The resolution includes a preamble citing historical precedents, including the United States Semiquincentennial Commission Act of 2016 (Public Law 114-196; 36 U.S.C. note prec. 101), which established the commission to plan the 250th-anniversary commemoration. It also references the 1976 Bicentennial and the 2019 Apollo 11 commemoration on the National Mall as precedents for lighting and projecting imagery on the Washington Monument.

The joint resolution does not amend existing provisions of the United States Code, nor does it provide any new permanent authority, appropriations, or regulatory mandates. It operates solely as a formal congressional request to an executive branch official and a directive to a House officer. The resolution was approved on December 2, 2025.
